purpose: Distinguish recoverable readout fit from changing the magnitude objective, conditional on frozen pretrained features.
train: Same sixteen uniformly spaced valid moving windows per recording; 45 recordings, 720 windows, 8 existing groups.
validation: All windows of all four validation recordings; one existing group, disjoint from train.

fixed.backbone: Pretrained parameters and BN buffers frozen; dropout disabled for feature extraction and evaluation.
fixed.head: Original 512-to-3 linear velocity head; identical initial head for both AdamW arms.
fixed.optimizer: Full-batch AdamW, lr=0.001, weight_decay=0, 256 updates per optimization arm.
fixed.selection: Final step 256 fixed in advance; no validation selection or tuning.
fixed.trajectory: Native stride-200 reconstruction, initial-position anchor, unaligned XYZ ATE, 10s RTE and P95.

arms.vector_mse: mean((prediction-target)^2), averaged over windows and three components.
arms.least_squares: Minimum-change head residual solve in float64 with rcond=1e-6; original vector MSE, no magnitude term.

acceptance: Train fit alone is insufficient; preserve paired full-validation ATE, 10s RTE and tail counterexamples.
A finite-budget optimizer comparison is not a proof that original training converged or that information is sufficient.
Least squares is a numerical readout control; rank truncation and overfitting remain limitations.
One validation group already used for checkpoint selection is not independent test accuracy or a general causal explanation.
